claims.text: Inngest's `step.run()` makes each call independently executed and retried; if an LLM call in step 3 of a document pipeline times out, only that step is retried without re-running validation or the first LLM call.
In Inngest, data returned from each step is persisted and automatically available to subsequent steps.

Inngest's pattern guidance is to break long-running jobs into discrete steps that each run independently, throw their own errors, retry on their own, and pass data to the next step, so a failure in an evaluation LLM call does not force re-running and re-paying for the first LLM call.
Inngest docs say Step Functions require defining workflows in a JSON DSL, and Temporal requires running its own server infrastructure and learning a framework-specific programming model.
DBOS.recv, called inside a workflow, durably waits for a message with a timeout (e.g. `DBOS.recv(timeout_seconds=TIMEOUT)`), allowing an agent to wait hours or days for human input.

In DBOS, the workflow's progress is checkpointed and both the deadline and the notification are stored in the database, so a waiting agent recovers and keeps waiting after server restarts or code upgrades until the notification arrives or the deadline is reached.

DBOS.send persists messages to the database, so if `send` completes successfully the destination workflow is guaranteed to receive it; it can be called from an HTTP endpoint to deliver human responses to an agent.
DBOS agents can publish status with DBOS.set_event (e.g. 'working', 'pending_approval', 'denied') and external code can read it with DBOS.get_event, letting a frontend show what an agent is doing.
DBOS's workflow introspection API (list_workflows with status PENDING) combined with get_event can be used to build an 'inbox' of all agents currently waiting for human input.

DBOS provides an agent inbox example application demonstrating human-in-the-loop, where DBOS.recv durably waits for a configurable time and recovers automatically from transient failures and process restarts.
Inngest stores each completed step's result, and when work resumes after a retry or wait, functions resume from the last completed step instead of from the start.
Inngest describes durable agents as workflows whose next step is chosen by a model, with each model call and tool call running as a step.
Inngest lets users set concurrency and other flow controls to protect services a workflow calls, and says runs can wait without holding compute.
Inngest offers 'Durable Endpoints', regular HTTP endpoints that return results as HTTP responses even after temporary errors and retries.

On Inngest, an agent is a loop of model calls and tool calls where each call runs in its own `step.run()`; a successful step's result is saved as a checkpoint, and completed steps return saved results instead of re-running when a step fails and is retried.
Inngest's `step.waitForEvent()` pauses an agent until a matching event arrives or a timeout passes, used for actions needing human approval.

Inngest uses step-level memoization for agent durability: every completed step (LLM call, tool invocation, side effect) has its result persisted, and on replay a stored result is injected rather than the call being re-made.
Every Inngest `step.run()` gets automatic retries with configurable policies for number of attempts, backoff strategy, and timeout.

Temporal's LangGraph Plugin (blog post dated Jul 16, 2026) runs a LangGraph graph as a Temporal Workflow, with each node able to execute as a Temporal Activity and execution checkpointed at every node.
With Temporal's LangGraph plugin, a failed step such as a model call timeout or tool error is retried per policy and the graph resumes from durable state on the same or a different worker.
Temporal supports human-in-the-loop agents through Signals & Updates and Queries.
In Temporal, Activities automatically retry LLM requests that fail due to network glitches or rate limiting, so developers don't write the retry logic themselves.
Temporal records a full Event History when executing a Workflow, which underpins its durability.

Restate automatically retries transient errors such as rate limits and network failures, persists steps (LLM calls, tools) to recover progress after failures, and suspends idle long-running agents to save costs.
Restate documents a Human Approval pattern: durable waiting for human decisions with crash-proof timeouts.
